principles: record software, environment, parameters, methods, inputs, outputs and provenance
automate experiments where practical and preserve raw observations
record random seeds and run-time parameters when randomized scheduling or timing is used
distinguish artifact functionality from independently reproduced results
do not promote blocked setup or absent fault injection to candidate PASS/FAIL

preExecutionAmendments.reason: Prevent mixing code revisions across round-robin repetitions or candidates; operationalizes the existing requirement to record software identity and provenance.
preExecutionAmendments.constraint: The T5/r1 lifecycle qualification support may originate from an earlier verified revision only while its candidate lifecycle-qualification hash remains current; every record admitted to one formal benchmark ledger must otherwise share one verified Git repository revision.

preExecutionAmendments.reason: Prevent formal repetitions from silently mixing execution environments or candidate runtime profiles while ignoring non-semantic per-run identities such as paths, ports, process IDs and container IDs.
preExecutionAmendments.constraint: Every READY record in one formal ledger must share one canonical common execution environment identity for OS, architecture, Node runtime and recorded package-manager identity; within each candidate, every READY record must also share one canonical candidate profile derived from candidate/source identity, adapter SHA-256, manifest and exact installed dependency versions, declared mode/authority boundary, lifecycle-qualification SHA-256 and stable observed native runtime identity. Dynamic workspace paths, ports, task queues, process IDs, container IDs and database URLs are excluded from identity.

preExecutionAmendments.reason: Prevent candidate adapters, runners or bridges from redefining semantic success and ensure formal verdicts remain traceable to raw observations under one acceptance authority per critical mutant.
preExecutionAmendments.constraint: Formal semantic acceptance for every benchmark-critical mutant must be computed by candidate-agnostic evaluator code from raw observations; candidate adapters and execution runners may translate native evidence but must not define or override success semantics. Fault injection is classified separately, and an absent intended fault remains INCONCLUSIVE. For T7 and T8, the frozen executable acceptance contract requires exactly one external apply, one stable semantic operation identity, reachable durable authority, objective_completed terminal recovery and COMPLETED final status; T7 additionally requires zero response losses, while T8 additionally requires that the measurement cutoff was not reached after the one required response-loss fault. RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED is observable evidence but is not T7/T8 PASS under this V1 contract.

preExecutionAmendments.reason: Prevent runtime-verified cleanup support obtained with one native runtime artifact from authorizing benchmark records executed with a different native runtime artifact under the same candidate/version label.
preExecutionAmendments.constraint: Any runtime-verified T5/r1 lifecycle qualification used to open formal cleanup support must record a SHA-256 identity of the stable native runtime identity observed in that qualification, and every READY formal benchmark record for that candidate must derive the same native runtime identity SHA-256 before ledger admission or benchmark eligibility. A lifecycle qualification produced with a different native runtime artifact cannot authorize formal benchmark records even when candidate version, Git revision policy and lifecycle-qualification source hash otherwise satisfy their independent gates.

executionOrder.reason: avoid completing all repetitions of one candidate before exposing later candidates to the same experimental window
executionOrder.sequence: for repetition 1..100, execute each critical mutant for each candidate using the declared environment profile; record any unavailable run as BLOCKED rather than substituting another configuration

promotionRules.pass: all predeclared acceptance checks true under executed intended fault
promotionRules.fail: at least one predeclared acceptance check false under executed intended fault
promotionRules.benchmarkEligibility: all six critical mutants must have at least 100 unique valid records and none may be BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE
